title: Which groups of primes do 112 and 84 share?
description: One hundred and twelve and eighty four are written as primes, one above the other. Groups of primes that sit in both are multiplied, one is added, and the biggest is the highest common factor. Keeko's doubt, that the smaller number is the highest common factor, is tested by fitting eighty four into one hundred and twelve.
teaching_notes: One idea: a group of shared primes can use a prime only as many times as both numbers have it. Watch for students who count three or four twos because one number has them.

source: Find the common factors and the HCF of 112 and 84 from their prime factorisations.
video_script.why: The child has found common groups for two numbers with each prime used once or twice, and now meets a prime that repeats four times in one number.
video_script.substitution: A group of shared primes can use a prime only as many times as both numbers have it; multiply the groups and add one.
video_script.anchor: One hundred and twelve and eighty four written as primes, one above the other.
video_script.wrong_answer: the highest common factor is eighty four
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the highest common factor is eighty four, the smaller number. But eighty four goes into one hundred and twelve only once and leaves a gap.
video_script.payoff_line: The highest common factor is twenty eight.

final_answer.spoken: the common factors are one, two, four, seven, fourteen and twenty eight, and the highest common factor is twenty eight

maths_rules: 84 has two 2s, so a shared group has at most two 2s. Groups in both: 2, 7, 2 x 2 = 4, 2 x 7 = 14, 2 x 2 x 7 = 28.
With 1, the common factors are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. The highest is 2 x 2 x 7 = 28 (112 / 28 = 4 and 84 / 28 = 3).
Slip: 84 goes into 112 once, with 112 - 84 = 28 left over, so 84 is not a factor of 112.
video_script.design: One idea: shared groups use a prime only as many times as both numbers have it. Assumes prime factorisation. Wrong idea: the smaller number is the HCF. The two factorisations stay on the board all video.
